newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Pick boosts exports by 32.7 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Pick boosts exports by 32.7 pct in 1996.

text.p: Hungarian meat processor company Pick Rt boosted its exports by 32.7 percent in forint terms last year, exceeding plans by 8.7 percent, the company said in its earnings report on Monday.
"Export sales also grew above expectations in dollar terms," Pick said.
The company's exports rose to $72.6 million in 1996 from $66.7 million in 1995, compared with an 1996 export plan of $70 million.
The higher-than-expected growth was partly due to a temporary rise in pork export subsidies, the company said.
"Seizing the opportunity, we increased the exports volume to 4,879 tonnes (in 1996) from a basis level of 2,083 tonnes (in 1995) and compared with the (1996) plan of 2,400 tonnes," Pick said.
Despite a drop in Hungarian real wages in 1996, domestic sales also grew by 14.5 percent, the company said.

Pick released its 1996 HAS preliminary results on Monday, reporting a 2.40 billion forint group net profit on net sales of 28.56 billion forints versus a 1995 group net profit of 1.82 billion forints on net sales of 23.64 billion forints.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Pick shares closed at 11,815 forints on Friday.
